bullets.text: Machine Learning (ML) is a subfield of Artificial Intelligence (AI).
ML systems learn patterns from data rather than being explicitly programmed.
Models improve over time with more data without needing reprogramming.
It's about teaching computers to learn from experience, similar to humans.
Machine learning is integrated into many aspects of daily life.
Examples include Netflix recommendations, spam filters, and virtual assistants (Siri/Alexa).
Also used in facial recognition, online shopping, and fraud detection systems.
Access to vast amounts of data generated constantly.
Increased computational power, especially with modern GPUs.
Development of sophisticated algorithms that extract insights effectively.
Most common type, trains models using labeled data (input + correct output).
Goal is to predict outputs for new, unseen inputs.
Example: Predicting house prices based on features and past sale prices.
Categorized into Regression (predicting continuous values) and Classification (predicting discrete labels).
Uses unlabeled data to discover patterns, relationships, or structures independently.
Clustering is a common application, grouping similar data points (e.g., customer segmentation).
Dimensionality reduction techniques simplify datasets by reducing features.
An agent learns by interacting with an environment and receiving feedback (rewards/penalties).
Goal is to learn a policy that maximizes total reward over time.
Examples include training robots to walk, game-playing AI (AlphaGo), and self-driving cars.
Data quality is crucial; noisy, biased, or incomplete data harms model performance.
Overfitting occurs when a model learns training data too well but fails on new data.
Ethical concerns arise from biased data leading to biased models with real-world consequences.
Understanding data context and model impact is as important as the algorithms.
Recap of ML definition, importance, three main types, and challenges.
Future lectures will delve deeper into specific algorithms and practical applications.
